text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Convicted rapists will be forced to pay victims N$10,000 in compensation and sentences will range from between five years and life imprisonment if the radical provisions of a new draft bill become law.
- Condemnation of ministers' plans to award themselves and other government and military top brass huge retirement packages has begun to surface.

- In public statements transport minister Hampie Plichta and Air Namibia director Johannes Gawaxab have rebuked an official of civil aviation for having claimed that over two thirds of the planes registered in Namibia are not airworthy.
- Yesterday's debate in the national council had to be adjourned early for the second time this week, because of a lack of a decision-making quorum.
- An elderly farmer of Bethanie in the south, Gerhardus Enslin (85) was murdered in cold blood on Tuesday afternoon.

- The ombudsman and the secretary-general of the Namibia national women's Organisation (Nanawo), as well as Nanawo president Netumbo Ndaitwah have crossed swords with their SWAPO colleague and MP Fidelis Sheyapo for his derogatory statements on women in the national council.

- The leakage of state documents revealing the benefits to be accorded to political office bearers upon retirement was strongly condemned by information minister Ben Amathila at this week's cabinet briefing.
- Warders at Windhoek Central Prison on Monday night launched a violent attack on trial-awaiting prisoners after the escape of five inmates, a fellow detainee has charged.
